summary: Our panel's 'BPC' resolves to PubChem CID 6620 (2,2-bis(4-hydroxy-3-methylphenyl)propane, dimethyl regioisomer, CAS 79-97-0) per PubChem's own synonym mapping. This compound has NO published ERalpha binding/activity data (only a CYP bioactivation/metabolism study). The compound the EDC toxicology field actually calls 'BPC' -- crystallized with ERalpha, ~410x more potent than BPA (IC50 ~2.7nM vs E2 ~0.88nM) via halogen-bonding from a dichloro-vinylidene bridge -- is a structurally different molecule, CAS 14868-03-2. A third, again different, ring-chlorinated propane-bridged compound (3,3'-dichloro-BPA) appears in Kitamura et al. 2005 with its own IC50 values. Score for CID 6620 is not validated by any of this literature.

summary: Riu 2011 reporter-gene assay: TCBPA and BPA both full ERalpha agonists with comparable potency (BPA EC50 0.29uM slightly lower/more potent than TCBPA 0.53uM) -- halogenation did not reduce ERalpha potency in this study. Pelch 2019, a larger panel study, instead found TCBPA only 21.3% max efficacy relative to E2, i.e. near-inactive at ERalpha. The two disagree, and neither supports TCBPA being clearly stronger than BPA.
